your_book:
Jaleel's book had a soft Friday. Most of the 18 holdings closed lower, and the book sits at -1.03% unrealized. The sharpest drops were Lululemon (-4.85%), On Holding (-4.38%), Novartis (-3.3%), Equifax (-2.55%), Adobe (-2.49%) and AutoZone (-2.14%). Abbott (+1.16%) was the main offset, and Rocket Lab bounced 2.69%. The chip names (NVIDIA -0.59%, Broadcom -0.48%) slipped on worries that AI-infrastructure funding is tight, with Jensen Huang pointing to a scarcity of capital. No headline was provided to explain On Holding's drop, so treat it as unexplained for now.

The drift is where price and thesis disagree. Headlines say software and financials rose on a rotation out of AI-exposed names, yet Adobe fell 2.49% and S&P Global slipped 0.62%. Adobe's flagged problem is narrative (AI-disruption fear), not numbers, and today fits that. Boston Scientific (9.5%) rates STRONG BUY at 79.2 QARP, but guidance was slashed, management guides flat through Q3, and the position is down 6.8%. Rocket Lab (5.7%) and Lululemon (3.8%) are both rated AVOID and are down 32.9% and 22.6%. Together they are 9.5% of the book, and a one-day bounce doesn't change that.

Watch Boston Scientific's report on Oct 28, then NVIDIA on Nov 17.
